source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Verbal threats should not be documented because reporting them can distort workplace safety statistics","B":"Only injuries requiring medical treatment provide useful information for violence-prevention programs","C":"Reporting supports pattern detection, risk assessment, investigation, and prevention of future escalation","D":"Incident records are unrelated to prevention because violence programs rely only on security staffing"}}
source_row.rationale: OSHA guidance encourages prompt reporting and recordkeeping of violent incidents, including threats. Reports help organizations assess hazards, investigate events, measure progress, and refine prevention strategies.
source_row.source_detail: Written program elements: prompt reporting of all violent incidents, recordkeeping, hazard assessment, and program evaluation; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: OSHA — Hospitals eTool: Workplace Violence Prevention
source_row.stem: Why should a healthcare workplace-violence program encourage reporting of threats and incidents even when no physical injury occurs?
